claims.location: characteristics[organism], characteristics[cell line], characteristics[cellosaurus accession], characteristics[cellosaurus name], characteristics[material type] all rows
claims.value: Homo sapiens / 143B cell / CVCL_2270 / 143B / cell line
claims.evidence: The samples are transmitochondrial cybrids: Paper Results: "Both cybrid clones, obtained from 143B TK− ρ° cells (King & Attadi, 1996a; King & Attardi, 1996b), were populated with mitochondria from the same heteroplasmic patient (Rana et al, 2000)"; Methods: "143B‐TK− osteosarcoma‐derived cybrid cells". The two clones (WT #4.1, Δ4-CYB #17.3E) have no Cellosaurus entry (search MT-CYB cybrid: 0 hits). The cell line / cellosaurus columns therefore name ONLY the nuclear parent 143B (CVCL_2270, synonym "143B TK-"; CLO:0001088 "143B cell"); this is made explicit by characteristics[cybrid nuclear parent], the mtDNA origin is given in characteristics[mitochondrial DNA donor], and the mtDNA genotype in characteristics[genotype]. (Cellosaurus models such cybrids as hybrid lines with two parents, e.g. GM16530 CVCL_IW03; no such entry exists for these clones.)

claims.location: characteristics[cybrid nuclear parent] all rows (custom column, campaign rule 15)
claims.evidence: Paper: "obtained from 143B TK− ρ° cells (King & Attardi 1996a,b)". The specific rho0 derivative is not named; Cellosaurus 143B.206 (CVCL_U923, King & Attardi rho0 line, HI CVCL_2270) is a plausible but unconfirmed candidate, so only the documented parent 143B CVCL_2270 is cited.

claims.location: characteristics[mitochondrial DNA donor] all rows (custom column, campaign rule 15)
claims.value: heteroplasmic MT-CYB 4-bp deletion patient, parkinsonism/MELAS overlap syndrome (de Coo 1999; Rana 2000)
claims.evidence: Paper: both clones "were populated with mitochondria from the same heteroplasmic patient (Rana et al, 2000)" - the WT clone carries the patient's wild-type mtDNA, the Δ4-CYB clone the mutant mtDNA, so the value is identical on WT and Δ4-CYB rows. de Coo 1999: heteroplasmic 4-bp MT-CYB deletion in a young boy with akinetic rigid syndrome and MELAS ("parkinsonism/MELAS overlap syndrome"); Rana 2000 isolated the cybrids from this patient.

claims.location: characteristics[organism part], characteristics[disease], characteristics[sex], characteristics[age], characteristics[developmental stage], characteristics[ancestry category] all rows
claims.value: femur / osteosarcoma / female / 13Y / 13-year-old stage / European ancestry
claims.evidence: These describe the NUCLEAR donor only, i.e. the donor of 143B (Cellosaurus CVCL_2270: SX Female, AG 13Y, DI Osteosarcoma, derived from site Bone, right femur UBERON_0000981, CC Population: Caucasian -> HANCESTRO:0005 European ancestry; 13Y -> HsapDv:0000107 13-year-old stage, not obsolete). They do not describe the mtDNA donor (a boy with parkinsonism/MELAS overlap syndrome, de Coo 1999), who is recorded in characteristics[mitochondrial DNA donor]. Disease choice: characteristics[disease] stays osteosarcoma (MONDO:0009807) on every row, matching the nuclear-parent cell line named in characteristics[cell line]/[cellosaurus accession]. A MELAS/parkinsonism term was not put on the Δ4-CYB rows because the WT clone derives from the SAME patient (paper: "the same heteroplasmic patient"), so the donor disease does not differ between arms; giving it to Δ4-CYB rows only would turn the mtDNA genotype into a disease contrast, and giving it to both rows would assign a mitochondrial disease to a clone carrying 100% wild-type mtDNA. The compared variable is captured by genotype; the donor syndrome is stated in the mtDNA-donor column.

claims.location: characteristics[cell type], characteristics[passage number] all rows
claims.evidence: Neither the paper nor Cellosaurus states a cell type for 143B or passage numbers of the cybrids.

claims.location: characteristics[culture medium] all rows
claims.evidence: Methods: "The cells used in the SILAC experiments were grown in DMEM for SILAC (Gibco) plus 10% dialyzed serum ... and 50 μg/ml uridine"; PRIDE: "grown in 'heavy' DMEM ... and in 'light' DMEM". NCIT:C185409.

claims.location: characteristics[cellular component] all rows
claims.evidence: Complexome: "Mitochondria isolated from 1:1 mixtures of differentially SILAC labeled ... cybrids"; IP: "Mitoplasts isolated from cells (0.5–2 mg) were resuspended in lysis-buffer" (PRIDE). GO:0005739 (mitoplasts are mitochondria without outer membrane; no closer GO cellular-component term).

claims.location: characteristics[genotype] and factor value[genotype] all rows
claims.evidence: Paper: "#17.3E Δ4‐CYB clone, homoplasmic for the 4‐bp deletion in MT‐CYB (heretofore referred to as Δ4‐CYB), in comparison with clone #4.1, containing 100% wild‐type (heretofore referred to as WT) mitochondrial DNA". Free text (custom characteristics column, campaign rule 15).

claims.location: comment[label] all rows
claims.evidence: Methods: light = K0/R0, heavy = L‐lysine‐13C6,15N2 (K8) and L‐arginine‐13C6,15N4 (R10); two-channel SILAC (multiplicity 2). Which genotype carries which label per run is documented in the channel-map claim.

claims.location: comment[technical replicate] all rows
claims.evidence: Each gel slice was injected once (one raw file per slice; no repeat injections in the file list).

claims.location: comment[data file], assay name all rows
claims.evidence: Every RAW entry of the PRIDE file list is listed once per SILAC channel (2 rows per file).

claims.location: comment[cleavage agent details] all rows
claims.evidence: PRIDE sample protocol: IP slices "digested with trypsin"; complexome slices "in-gel digested with trypsin". Search enzyme rule not recorded in the deposited outputs.

claims.location: comment[proteomics data acquisition method] all rows
claims.evidence: Q Exactive Plus method in the HACYC1 raw headers: "Full MS / dd-MS² (TopN)", TopN 10; LTQ Orbitrap XL complexome runs: PD/Mascot PSMs of data-dependent CID MS2 scans (method T10_FTIT_CID).

claims.location: comment[precursor mass tolerance], comment[fragment mass tolerance] all rows
claims.evidence: No search parameter file (mqpar.xml, PD .msf/.pdResult, Mascot .dat) is deposited and neither the paper nor PRIDE states tolerances. (Observed PSM delta masses in the complexome tables lie within -10.08..+9.96 ppm, suggestive of a 10 ppm Mascot window, but this is not a stated parameter.)

claims.value: v1.1.0 / ms-proteomics v1.2.0, human v1.1.0, cell-lines v1.1.0 / NT=sdrf-skills;VV=v0.1.0
claims.evidence: Campaign rules 1 and 10; ms-proteomics latest 1.2.0 per upstream templates.yaml line 150.

claims.location: source name, comment[label], characteristics[biological replicate], characteristics[detergent], factor value[detergent], comment[sample preparation batch], all 512 rows (channel map)
claims.value: A1-A64 (MultiConsensus_psms.txt) = DDM rep1, WT heavy / Δ4-CYB light; A65-A128 (laneC) = DDM rep2, WT light / Δ4-CYB heavy; A130-A192+A257 (lane3) = digitonin rep1, WT heavy / Δ4-CYB light; A193-A256 (lane4) = digitonin rep2, WT light / Δ4-CYB heavy
claims.evidence: Explicit: two reciprocal-labelling experiments per detergent ("This experiment was performed in duplicate using reciprocal labeling"; "Differentially labeled mitochondria solubilized with either 4 mg digitonin ... or 1.6 mg DDM/mg protein were resolved by BNGE ... Each lane was excised in 64, 1‐mm‐thick slices"); Fig EV1 legend: a "DDM‐solubilized" experiment "where Δ4‐CYB cells were labeled with the heavy (H) amino acids" and a "digitonin‐solubilized" experiment "where WT cells were labeled with the heavy (H) amino acids". Lane -> file block from the "Spectrum File" column of the four PSM tables (each covers exactly 64 raws). Orientation per lane from the data (orient.py): MT-CYB peptides, not translated in Δ4-CYB (Fig 2B), occur only in one channel (A1-64: 4 heavy/0 light; laneC 6 light/0 heavy; lane3 17 heavy/0 light; lane4 20 light/0 heavy), corroborated by UQCRC1 (103 H/1 L; 399 L/0 H; 429 H/0 L; 452 L/0 H) and UQCRFS1. Detergent per lane from the data: in the WT channel the cIII2 subunit UQCRC1 co-migrates with cI NDUFS1 (supercomplexes, retained by digitonin, dissociated by DDM) in lane3 and lane4 (profile overlap 0.66/0.67) but not in A1-64 and laneC (0.06/0.07); this assignment is also the only one consistent with Fig EV1 (DDM with Δ4-CYB heavy = laneC; digitonin with WT heavy = lane3) and pairs the lanes by MS run dates (180213/180219 vs 180307/180313). Biological replicate numbers restart per (genotype, detergent) group: rep1 = the WT-heavy mixture, rep2 = the reciprocal mixture.

claims.location: comment[fraction identifier] all rows
claims.evidence: Rule 16 consideration: the BN-PAGE slices are gel fractions of ONE solubilized SILAC mixture per lane, each slice measured once; the 64 slices together reconstruct that lane (complexome profiles along the lane, Figs 3/5/EV1-5; Fig 2A pools all slices for H/L ratios). They are not independently prepared biochemical samples compared as conditions (unlike the sucrose-gradient precedent PXD004650), so they are encoded as comment[fraction identifier] with the slice order preserved, which keeps per-slice profiles reconstructable and lets pooled quantification group the 64 files per source. BN-PAGE lanes cut into 64 slices; fraction = rank of the slice number in the raw name (-CybMCo-<slice>-) within the lane. Lane digitonin rep1 holds slices 142-205; slice 205 was acquired as PRO4052A257 (run date 180309) and is the 64th file the lane3 PSM table lists; there is no PRO4052A129 in the deposit.

claims.location: comment[fractionation method] all rows
claims.evidence: Blue-native PAGE lanes cut into 64 slices. CHMO:0002276 blue native PAGE is not a descendant of PRIDE:0000550, so the nearest PRIDE fractionation term "Gel electrophoresis" is used.

claims.location: comment[instrument], comment[dissociation method], comment[collision energy], comment[ms2 mass analyzer] all rows
claims.value: NT=LTQ Orbitrap XL;AC=MS:1000556 / NT=collision-induced dissociation;AC=MS:1000133 / 35 NCE / NT=linear ion trap;AC=MS:1000291
claims.evidence: Raw headers of PRO4052A1, A65, A130, A193, A257: "LTQ Orbitrap XL MS"; method T10_FTIT_CID_5K40-56-90B_Lockmass ("Activation Type: CID", "Normalized Coll. Energy: 35.0"); FT survey / IT MS2 per the method name; PSM tables "Activation Type" CID, "MS Order" MS2 for all 407,560 PSMs read. PRIDE data protocol: "LTQ XL‐Orbitrap system".

claims.location: comment[modification parameters] all rows (6 columns)
claims.value: Label:13C(6)15N(2) K, Label:13C(6)15N(4) R, Oxidation M, Propionamide C, Acetyl Protein N-term, Formyl Protein N-term, all Variable
claims.evidence: Modifications observed in the Mascot PSM tables (orient.py): K(Label:13C(6)15N(2)), R(Label:13C(6)15N(4)), M(Oxidation), C(Propionamide), N-Term(Acetyl), N-Term(Formyl). Propionamide is variable (1,529 of 2,695 Cys-containing PSMs in MultiConsensus_psms.txt carry fewer Propionamide sites than Cys residues); labels are variable per campaign rule 11 and PRIDE ("Mascot was configured to consider the possibility of the presence of the appropriate heavy-labeled amino acid residues"). Acetyl/Formyl PP=Protein N-term inferred from the full PSM tables (nterm.py against UniProt human reviewed): 15,542 of 15,715 N-Term(Acetyl) PSMs and 5,005 of 5,062 N-Term(Formyl) PSMs map to protein position 1/2 (155 and 35 not found in Swiss-Prot, 18 and 22 only internal - isoform/TrEMBL candidates); the Mascot setting itself is not deposited.

limitations: Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500; the paper was read from the PMC Open Access S3 copy (PMC6996572.1 txt/xml/figures).

Search tolerances are not deposited for either search (PD/Mascot complexome, MaxQuant IP); comment[precursor/fragment mass tolerance] = not available, so parse_sdrf convert-openms cannot convert the file (campaign precedent PXD014368/PXD006676).
The Δ4-CYB clone number conflicts in the paper (Results: #17.3E used for all figures; Methods complexome paragraph: "#17.1 Δ4‐CYB"); no clone number is written to the SDRF.

Cybrids are not in Cellosaurus; 143B (CVCL_2270) is recorded as the nuclear parent only. Sex, age, developmental stage, ancestry, organism part and osteosarcoma describe the 143B (nuclear) donor; the mtDNA donor (same heteroplasmic MT-CYB Δ4 patient for both clones; male, parkinsonism/MELAS overlap, de Coo 1999) is given in characteristics[mitochondrial DNA donor]. The 143B TK− ρ° derivative used to make the cybrids is not named (143B.206, CVCL_U923, is a plausible but unconfirmed candidate). A second mutant clone #17.3B appears only in Fig 1C; clone E (#17.3E) was used for all later figures.

Lane-to-detergent and lane-to-orientation assignments are data-derived (MT-CYB/UQCRC1 channel presence; cIII2–cI co-migration) and cross-checked against the Fig EV1 legend; no deposited table names the lanes. Whether the DDM and digitonin lanes of the same orientation come from the same mitochondrial preparation is not stated; replicate numbers therefore restart per detergent group and make no cross-detergent identity claim.

Acetyl/Formyl position (Protein N-term) is inferred from the PSM data, not read from a Mascot parameter file. The MaxQuant re-quantification of the DDM complexome (Fig 2A, "logarithmic ratios were calculated using MaxQuant") is not deposited; this SDRF follows the deposited PD/Mascot search.
The gel image 180206gelcomplexomic004.tif (non-MS file) is not represented.
